mutations.before: const briefFetchKey = brief === undefined || cell === undefined ? undefined : previewFetchKey(brief, cell.productId);
mutations.because: CC2's fix is keying the fetch on the brief's CONTENT (previewFetchKey), not its object identity. Restoring identity as the key reintroduces the defect: toBrief(state) builds a new brief object on every keystroke, so a look-preserving edit (typing in targetAudience) fires a fresh /preview-frame request again. Caught by a CALL COUNT, not a mount count.

isRailWideEnough is the JS-side mirror of the row's own CSS container query (CC2): below 56rem the rail is CSS-hidden but stays mounted, and withholding `brief` is the only thing that stops usePreviewFrame from building a request there. Feeding the dock `previewBrief` unconditionally lets a rail nobody can see keep fetching. Caught by a CALL COUNT ("nothing fetches below the breakpoint"), not a mount count — the rail's own mount is unaffected by this mutation.

previewBrief is deliberately memoised on a narrower key than draftBrief (CC1/CC2's memo boundary) so the preview dock and its fetch can bail out on a look-preserving keystroke. The YAML view is the rail's read-only SECOND view (D61) and must stay live: feeding it the memoised previewBrief instead of the live draftBrief makes it go stale on exactly the fields the memo key ignores (e.g. targetAudience). Caught by a staleness ASSERTION on rendered content, not a call count or a mount count.

The JS-side breakpoint and the CSS container query (`[@container(min-width:56rem)]:flex`, BriefEditor.tsx) are two independent literals with nothing enforcing agreement between them -- mutating the constant alone (never touching the CSS) reproduces exactly the silent-drift gap a reviewer found: every OTHER test stays green because each side was previously asserted against itself, not against the other. Caught by a parity assertion that derives one value from the other (parses the rem out of the rail's own className, multiplies by the 16px root, compares to the constant) -- not a call count, not a mount count, and not a plain literal-equality check on either side alone.

A `"use client"` component (BriefEditor.tsx) is still prerendered on the server at Next build time, and a useState initializer runs during that server render, where there is no `window`. A first version of this seed had no guard here and reasoned (wrongly) that only client chrome calls it; it broke `yarn build` with `ReferenceError: window is not defined` prerendering /brief/new -- a failure only CI's build step could see, since happy-dom always provides a `window`. Removing the guard here reproduces exactly that: `initialMinInlineSizeSeed` throws instead of seeding `false` once `window` is genuinely absent. Caught HERE by a unit test that stubs `window` to `undefined` for one assertion (`vi.stubGlobal`) and expects `false`, not a throw -- so the suite itself catches it, not only CI's build.

previewFetchKey is a pure CONTENT fingerprint (product colour/logo, message, style, template, platforms, sizes, timeline, background source, duration) and rawRailProps carries the campaign name, never the id -- neither term names WHICH creative is previewed. Without the identity axis, two saved briefs sharing every visual input but a different id produce the SAME key, so BriefEditor's memo keeps handing PreviewDock the OLD brief and usePreviewFrame's own identity guard (identityAxis = identityKey ?? brief.id) never sees the switch it exists to catch (FI1's defect, #448, reintroduced narrower). Caught by an ASSERTION that the stale frame clears when the previewed brief's id changes -- not a call count, not a mount count.
